- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points below true peak in next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after strong upward moves, underestimates after strong downward moves — adjust by smoothing out extreme deviations from 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price in early days (1–7) of forecast window — apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5 points for first 5 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a dip, model often misses the rally — add 1–2 points to forecast if sentiment >0.75 and price is below 10% from recent high.
